indexes: chunk directory over sorted canonical triple bytes (subject prefix)
engines.name: chunked_binary

query_plans.predicate_object: full scan of every chunk (no secondary index)
query_plans.subject: binary search the chunk directory, scan forward while the 0x83+subject prefix matches

engines.schema: magic IDCB 00 01; chunks of u32-BE-length-framed canonical triples, at most 4096 bytes; directory of (u64 offset, u32 length, first triple); trailer (u64 directory offset, u32 chunk count, IDCB)

engines.name: redb_tuple

query_plans.predicate_object: range scan of pos from tuple prefix bytes(predicate).bytes(object)
query_plans.subject: range scan of spo from tuple prefix bytes(subject)

engines.schema: tables spo and pos: TableDefinition<&[u8], ()>; key = id_core::tuple bytes(s).bytes(p).bytes(o) (pos: p, o, s) over canonical term bytes

engines.durability: journal_mode DELETE, synchronous FULL (defaults) on every commit
indexes: triples_spo unique expression index (sk, pk, ok)
engines.name: sqlite_jsonb

query_plans.predicate_object: SEARCH triples USING INDEX triples_po (<expr>=? AND <expr>=?)
query_plans.subject: SEARCH triples USING INDEX triples_spo (<expr>=?)

engines.durability: journal_mode DELETE, synchronous FULL (defaults) on every commit; deleted triples leave their interned terms
engines.name: sqlite_blob_rows

query_plans.predicate_object: SEARCH tp USING COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_terms_1 (bytes=?); SEARCH tobj USING COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_terms_1 (bytes=?); SEARCH t USING COVERING INDEX triples_pos (p=? AND o=?); SEARCH ts USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)
query_plans.subject: SEARCH ts USING COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_terms_1 (bytes=?); SEARCH t USING PRIMARY KEY (s=?); SEARCH tp USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?); SEARCH tobj USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)

engines.select_all: SELECT ts.bytes, tp.bytes, tobj.bytes FROM triples t JOIN terms ts ON ts.id = t.s JOIN terms tp ON tp.id = t.p JOIN terms tobj ON tobj.id = t.o

limits: single machine, single process, one thread; timings are wall-clock microseconds for the given build profile and are only comparable within one run
corpus is synthetic (about 6000 triples, 1000 subjects); production graphs may differ in size, skew and term mix
durability differs by engine: chunked_binary does not fsync, redb and SQLite fsync on each commit with their default settings
chunked_binary has no secondary index, so predicate/object queries scan the whole file and every write rewrites it
sqlite_blob_rows never collects interned terms whose triples were deleted
storage bytes depend on the pinned engine versions and page sizes; other versions or settings may differ
